newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kurds say they killed three Iraqi officers.
newsitem.headline: Kurds say they killed three Iraqi officers.

text.p: Kurdish guerrillas said they beat back on Tuesday an attack by rival guerrillas directed by the Iraqi military in northern Iraq, killing more than 50 people including three Iraqi officers.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) said in a statement issued in Paris the attack involved a combined force of Iraqi auxiliary units and guerrillas of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
It said the four-pronged attack was launched with artillery and rocket support near Mawat, east of Sulaimaniya.
PUK identified the three dead Iraqi officers as Khalil Thahir of the Mukhabarat Service, Simlko Hameed of the Public Security Service, and Ayob Namiq of the Military Intelligence Service.
PUK had said on Monday that a member of the Iraqi military intelligence was killed in a weekend clash in the same area.
It said Iraqi intelligence and army officers dressed in Kurdish gear were actively engaged in planning and directing a KDP offensive against PUK forces.
KDP guerrillas backed by Iraqi forces launched an offensive against the PUK last month, prompting the United States to fire missiles at Iraq and extend a no-fly zone in the south of the country.
